Definition: probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage:--Scythian.
BiblicalUsage: The Scythian stands in Paul's list of all the divisions that vanish in Christ: neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free. The Scythians were counted the wildest of outsiders, and Paul names them last to make the point complete.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that no one is too far out for Christ to bring in, and if the Scythian belongs, then nobody is beyond the reach of the gospel.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
